title: Air Conditioning (A/C) Compressor Belt
introduction:
The air conditioning (A/C) compressor belt carries rotation from the crankshaft pulley to the compressor, which circulates refrigerant. This procedure applies to your 5.0L 32V engine with twin independent variable camshaft timing (Ti-VCT). Removal involves cutting and discarding the belt; installation uses a cable tie to guide the belt onto the crankshaft pulley. Keeping the belt above the oil pan flange prevents the belt and engine damage identified in the installation notice.

**Source wording clarification:** The belt-positioning text calls the ribs “accessory drive belt” ribs, but the accompanying original pictures show the separate A/C belt being positioned between the compressor and crankshaft pulleys. The main accessory belt has already been removed. Here, those positioning instructions explicitly name the A/C belt to match the illustrated component. The source also prints “tensioned” where the corresponding belt-routing instruction identifies the tensioner. Its later accessory-belt seating check is an after-installation check; keep it in mind when that belt is refitted. [Compare the original wording and illustrations](/source/G1688134.pdf).

items.name: Cable Ties
items.detail: For installation, use a cable tie with a minimum width of 3 mm (0.12 in).

items.name: Replacement A/C compressor belt
items.detail: Removal cuts and discards the old belt, so have the replacement for this engine ready before starting.

items.name: Access to the A/C compressor belt
items.detail: Remove the air cleaner outlet pipe, then the accessory drive belt, using the referenced 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT procedures.

edits.text: Special tools and general equipment
Removal

NOTICE: Never lubricate the A/C compressor belt, accessory drive belt, tensioner or pulleys. Lubrication can damage the belt material and the tensioner damping mechanism. Do not put any fluids or belt dressing on the A/C compressor belt, accessory drive belt or pulleys.

Remove the air cleaner outlet pipe.

See: [Air Cleaner Outlet Pipe](#/document/G1675684) (303-12C Intake Air Distribution and Filtering - 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Taking the pipe out of the way gives you access for the belt work.

edits.text:
Remove the accessory drive belt.

See: [Accessory Drive Belt](#/document/G1688132) (303-05C Accessory Drive - 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Removing this belt clears the crankshaft pulley area for work on the A/C compressor belt.

edits.text: Cut through the A/C compressor belt, then discard it.
edits.why: Cutting frees the belt from the pulleys.

edits.text: Installation
NOTE: Check that the A/C compressor belt is seated correctly on the A/C compressor pulley.
Position the A/C compressor belt in the following 3 stages.
Stage 1: Pass the A/C compressor belt between the crankshaft pulley and the accessory drive belt tensioner.
edits.why: The source prints “accessory drive belt tensioned.” This names the tensioner shown at the belt-routing gap, consistent with the corresponding instruction beside the same original positioning illustration in the 3.7L procedure.

edits.text: Stage 2: Move the A/C compressor belt behind the crankshaft pulley, keeping the belt’s ribs facing toward the front of the vehicle.
edits.why: The source calls these “accessory drive belt ribs.” The original positioning picture shows the A/C belt being handled; that is the belt identified explicitly here. The rib direction is unchanged.

edits.text: Stage 3: Fit the A/C compressor belt onto the A/C compressor pulley as illustrated. Keep the lower section of this belt above the oil pan, with its ribs facing toward the front of the vehicle.
edits.why: Again, the source uses “accessory drive belt ribs” while describing and picturing the A/C belt. Follow the pictured A/C-belt position, including its path above the oil pan.

edits.text: NOTE: After installation, check that the A/C compressor belt is seated correctly on both the crankshaft pulley and the A/C compressor pulley.

Place the A/C compressor belt over the top of the crankshaft pulley. Feed a cable tie with a minimum width of 3 mm (0.12 in) through the crankshaft pulley spokes, then up and over the A/C compressor belt. Tighten the cable tie.

General equipment: Cable Ties.
edits.why: The cable tie holds the belt against the crankshaft pulley so pulley rotation can draw the belt into place.

edits.text: NOTICE: Keep the A/C compressor belt above the oil pan flange. If it is not above the flange, the A/C compressor belt and engine can be damaged.
With the A/C compressor belt above the oil pan flange, turn the crankshaft clockwise by hand 180°.
edits.why: Crankshaft rotation draws the belt onto the pulley; keeping the belt above the flange avoids the interference identified in the notice.

edits.text: Remove the cable tie. Turn the crankshaft clockwise by hand 360° and verify that the A/C compressor belt is seated correctly on the crankshaft and A/C compressor pulleys.
edits.why: Turning by hand lets you check how the belt tracks on both pulleys after the temporary tie is removed.

edits.text: After installation, check that the accessory drive belt is seated correctly on every pulley.
edits.why: This is an after-installation check to apply when the accessory belt is refitted below. The image accompanying this source instruction depicts the separate A/C belt, whose seating you have just checked; it does not replace the stated accessory-belt check.

edits.text:
Install the accessory drive belt.

See: [Accessory Drive Belt](#/document/G1688132) (303-05C Accessory Drive - 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: This restores the belt connection to the other belt-driven accessories.

edits.text:
Install the air cleaner outlet pipe.

See: [Air Cleaner Outlet Pipe](#/document/G1675684) (303-12C Intake Air Distribution and Filtering - 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Refitting the pipe restores the intake-air connection opened for access.

clarificationEvidence.positioning: Original photograph E185461 shows the A/C belt behind the crankshaft pulley and across the compressor pulley, with the lower belt ribs facing forward above the oil pan.
clarificationEvidence.installation: Original illustrations E186233/E186234 preserve clockwise hand rotation, 180°/360°, and the belt above the oil pan flange.
clarificationEvidence.componentName: The same positioning image and the 3.7L source instruction support correcting tensioned to tensioner; no different routing is introduced.
clarificationEvidence.seatingCheck: Original E186235 depicts the A/C belt. The source accessory-belt check remains an after-installation instruction, and the accessory belt installation stays in its original position.
